{{Short description|Norwegian chemist and businessman}}
[[File:Alf Bjorseth.jpg|thumb|Alf Bjørseth]]
'''Alf Bjørseth''' (born 24 November 1941) is a Norwegian chemist and businessperson in the energy sector.

He hails from [[Gamle Oslo]]. After [[examen artium|finishing]] his secondary education in 1960, he took the [[cand.real.]] degree at the [[University of Oslo]] in 1969. He was subsequently employed at [[SINTEF|SI]] and took his [[dr.philos.]] degree in 1979.<ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Alf Bjørseth|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|url=https://www.snl.no/Alf_Bjørseth|language=Norwegian|accessdate=27 December 2021}}</ref>

After spending the years 1980 to 1982 as research director at SI, he started a career in the industry sector. He was vice executive of Deminex from 1982 to 1984, director of research at [[Norsk Hydro]] from 1984 to 1990 and director of technology at [[Elkem]] from 1990 to 1994. In 1994 he founded the company ScanWafer, later [[Renewable Energy Corporation|REC]]. In 2005 he founded Norsun, then sold his shares in REC, and founded [[Scatec]].<ref name=snl/>

Bjørseth was decorated with [[Norwegian Chemical Society]]'s Guldberg and Waage Medal in 2003 and became Commander of the [[Order of St. Olav]] in 2006.<ref name=snl/> He is a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dnva.no/medlemmer/15|title=Norske medlemmer|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=no|access-date=27 December 2021}}</ref> and the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]].
